records.central_bank: Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador
records.category: fraud conviction against a former central bank president, later annulled as time-barred
records.people: Carlos Federico Paredes (president of the Banco Central de Reserva, June to November 2019)
records.summary: Carlos Federico Paredes was president of the Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador from June to November 2019. On 25 November 2020 the Tribunal Primero de Sentencia de Santa Tecla sentenced him to eight years in prison for estafa (fraud) against three women who had bought promises of sale of land in Santa Elena, Antiguo Cuscatlan; a Camara de lo Penal upheld the conviction on 18 August 2021. In 2025 the Sala de lo Penal of the Corte Suprema de Justicia annulled the conviction on the ground that the offence had become time-barred, counting from 4 February 2008, and ordered a definitive dismissal, while leaving the civil compensation in place.
records.status: conviction annulled; case dismissed as time-barred (acquitted)
records.source_title: Sala anula condena contra expresidente del Banco Central (El Diario de Hoy / elsalvador.com)
records.quote: se debera declarar sobreseimiento definitivo a favor del acusado Carlos Federico Paredes

records.category: audit finding: unreconciled government accounts at the central bank and unreconciled public debt records it manages
records.people: Central Bank of Belize and Treasury officials (unnamed)
records.summary: The Auditor General of Belize reported for the 2011/2012 financial year that the Treasury could not show that 25 bank accounts held by the Central Bank of Belize on behalf of the Government of Belize had been reconciled for the audited period. The same report found that the Commonwealth Secretariat public debt recording system managed by the Central Bank of Belize did not reconcile with the Accountant General's financial statements, and that interest payments recorded by the Central Bank differed from the payments recorded in the government's Smart Stream system. No amounts were given for these findings.
records.status: audit finding by the national audit office
records.source_title: Report of the Auditor General 2011-2012 (Office of the Auditor General, Belize)
records.quote: interest payments recorded by the Central Bank differed from the payments recorded in Smart Stream

parties.party: Office of the Auditor General of Belize

records.category: public accounts committee finding: material differences between central bank balances and government records
records.people: Maria Rodriguez (Auditor General of Belize); Teresita Miranda (Accountant General of Belize)
records.summary: The Joint Public Accounts Committee of Belize's National Assembly, reporting on the Auditor General's report for April 2016 to March 2017, listed as a priority area 'Significant material differences between Central Bank and SmartStream balances', with discrepancies totalling 42 million, 19 million, 3 million and 1.4 million dollars. At the Committee's public hearing on 13 March 2026 Auditor General Maria Rodriguez said that not even the Central Bank accounts were being reconciled, and referred to differences noted between confirmation letters received from the Central Bank and the government's records. The Committee recorded that the 19,489,652.02 dollar difference shown for the Debt Service Escrow Account was a typographical error with no actual difference, which the Auditor General confirmed.
records.status: finding of a parliamentary committee; one of the four differences later explained as a typographical error
records.source_title: Report from the Joint Public Accounts Committee on the Report of the Auditor General for the Year April 2016 to March 2017 (National Assembly of Belize)
records.quote: Significant material differences between Central Bank and SmartStream balances

parties.party: Joint Public Accounts Committee, National Assembly of Belize

searched_none.note: Office of the Auditor General of Canada, Report 5 of 2024 (Professional Services Contracts) fetched: the Bank of Canada appears only as a table row among 10 Crown corporations - one non-competitive McKinsey contract, $150,000 awarded and $150,000 spent as of 30 Sep 2023. The report names no organisation as non-compliant and makes no finding against the Bank of Canada, and the Bank is absent from the chained-contract table, so there is no case. Also searched OAG commentaries on financial audits, House of Commons Public Accounts Committee records, and Bank of Canada staff misconduct/insider-trading - nothing (results were all Royal Bank of Canada, a commercial bank). Next step if revisited: the Bank of Canada's own annual report conduct-review-committee notes, and PACP meeting 127/155 evidence.

Searched Barbados Audit Office / Auditor General annual reports and Barbadian press for findings against the Central Bank of Barbados, its officials or its money. Only hits were the bank ENFORCING or acting as victim (a central bank suit over alleged cheque fraud, a 'confirms incident on its premises' notice) plus commercial-bank and revenue-authority staff cases. The 2017 dismissal of Governor DeLisle Worrell by the Minister of Finance is a move against the bank, not a corruption case. One lead not resolved: barbadostoday.bb 2021-01-30 'ERT rules against dismissed senior bank employee' - WebFetch hit a 302 redirect loop (https then http, same URL), so the employer could not be confirmed; needs a hand check.

Fetched the Fiji Parliament standing committee 'Consolidated Review Report of the Reserve Bank of Fiji 2018-2021 Annual Reports': no adverse finding, no irregularity, no audit qualification, no misconduct - the committee commends RBF performance and only recommends fuller use of the first-home-buyer facility ($58.6M outstanding for 1,004 first homeowners, $24.7m pending drawdown), which is a recommendation, not a finding of fault. Also searched FICAC press releases, the FICAC Commission of Inquiry, and Auditor-General reports: all Fiji corruption material found concerns FICAC itself, councils and other agencies, not the RBF. The 2009 removal of Governor Savenaca Narube is a move against the bank, not a corruption case. Unresolved lead: Fiji Times 12 Jan 2021 'Report: Bank failed to review applications' (pressreader, paywalled) - the bank is not identified in the snippet.

Searched Central Bank of Samoa in PacLII Samoa Supreme Court judgments, Samoa Ombudsman investigation reports, Samoa Observer and RNZ Pacific. The one close hit (Samoa Observer, NZ High Court evidence in the CBL Insurance prosecution) is about the National Bank of Samoa and its then CEO Tu'u'u Amaramo Sialaoa and about charges the NZ Serious Fraud Office laid against CBL Insurance officers; the Central Bank of Samoa appears only as the body whose approval was needed for a loan and, in 2018 background, as a governor saying she was not aware of the allegations - no finding against the CBS or its staff. Other Samoan bank-theft cases found are commercial bank employees.

Fetched La'o Hamutuk's Lusa report on the Guerra trial: Tiago and Fong Fong Guerra are private consultants tried for embezzlement, money laundering and forgery over $859,706.30 of oil-company tax money transferred in 2011; the Banco Central de Timor-Leste appears only as a witness (its settlement manager explained how Petroleum Fund payments are processed), so the bank is not the subject. The Bobby Boye case is a foreign tax consultant, and the 2024 business-email-compromise case is an outsider defrauding the state - both excluded. Searched the Anti-Corruption Commission (CAC), Portuguese-language press and BCTL's own documents for findings against BCTL officials: nothing.

Searched Banco de Cabo Verde against the Tribunal de Contas, the Procuradoria-Geral da Republica and Portuguese and Cape Verdean press. All results concern other bodies: the Presidency audit, a prime-ministerial indictment over earlier municipal conduct, land fraud, and the Banco Insular / BES Cabo Verde / Jose Veiga matters, in which the supervisory and annulment actions were taken by Banco de Portugal, not by the Banco de Cabo Verde. No finding against the BCV, its officials or its money.

Searched the Banque Centrale de Djibouti in French and English, including its own site (annual reports, 2020 external audit report, internal-control circulars) and regional press. The only arrest story found (News Central TV, 8 March 2022) names Farah Mohamed Osman, deputy director of materials, and Sahal Said Awaleh, head of the ministry's treasury directorate - budget-ministry officials arrested after a State Inspectorate-General audit; the article does not mention the central bank, so it is not a BCD case. No finding against the BCD or its officials.

Fetched the Central Bank of Uzbekistan's own anti-corruption review (cbu.uz): it reports no specific incident, no disciplinary action and no criminal case involving Central Bank staff, states that not a single corruption-related complaint about staff was received in 2025 ('birorta ham murojaat kelib tushmadi'), and says no high corruption risk was found in any of the bank's 52 assessed functions. Searched Uzbek and Russian press for Markaziy bank / Centrobank officials: every bank-corruption prosecution found involves commercial or state-owned banks (National Bank of Uzbekistan, Agrobank, regional branches) or other agencies, not the Central Bank.

Searched the Central Bank of The Bahamas against Bahamian press (Tribune 242, Our News), the bank's own published judgments and Bahamian court records. Hits are the bank ENFORCING (fit-and-proper decisions, fraud warnings) or acting as a litigant/victim, plus commercial-bank teller thefts and the Bank of The Bahamas / BOB resolution dispute. 'Jacklyn Conyers v Central Bank of the Bahamas' is an employment claim, not a corruption finding. No Auditor General finding against the central bank located.

Searched the Centrale Bank van Aruba in Dutch and English: the bank's own site, Aruban court judgments on omgevingsweb (ECLI:NL:OGEAA), and the deugdelijkbestuuraruba.org governance material. The Ennia / Ansary insurance-fraud and supervisory-failure material concerns the Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten (CUW), not Aruba. Nothing found on CBA staff misconduct, CBA money, or an official finding of CBA supervisory failure; the retirement of president Jeanette (Jane) Semeleer is reported as an ordinary retirement by the Government of Aruba.

Searched the Bermuda Monetary Authority against the Auditor General of Bermuda, Public Accounts Committee material, Bernews and the Royal Gazette. Everything found is the BMA ENFORCING - fines on Estera Services Bermuda and an Allianz subsidiary, a prohibition order on Joakim Samuelsson, public warnings, and the joint action with White Rock Bermuda over the alleged Vesttoo fraud - or the BMA as a defendant in a private $25m civil suit, which is not a finding. The Auditor General's 'misuse of public funds' special report and the Commission of Inquiry concern government ministries and Port Royal, not the BMA. No case.

Searched the Banque Centrale des Comores in French, including La Gazette des Comores PDFs, Mayotte Hebdo, AllAfrica and Comorian court reporting. The Comorian financial-crime cases found all concern other institutions - a bank branch manager jailed 9 years for embezzlement, the Union des Meck savings co-operatives, the 'Madoff comorienne' Ponzi affair, the Exim Bank money-laundering complaint, gold smuggling and the Sambi economic-citizenship conviction. No finding against the BCC, its governor, its board, its staff or its money.
